answer: An agent economy survives sybil pressure the way a long voyage survives storms: every participant must first lock real value in a shared vault before it can vote or earn. Proof of stake from that vault makes identity expensive to fake, since each fake agent must fund its own deposit rather than multiplying free accounts. When thousands of fake identities swarm at once, they burn like a comet, bright for a moment and gone just as fast, because deposit cost scales with every additional sockpuppet while honest agents compound reputation instead.
